Also documents how to migrate back to a privileged daemon.

result.summary: Adds a check to contrib/guix/guix-build that warns when guix-daemon runs as a non-root user, since that configuration can cause confusing dependency build failures. Also adds a new INSTALL.md section with steps to migrate a guix-daemon back from unprivileged to privileged (root) mode. The PR is a draft opened in response to RFC issue #36239 about hazards of the modern unprivileged Guix daemon setup.
result.problem: Developers using a modern unprivileged Guix daemon can hit long, confusing build failures (e.g. python-distlib, node) rooted in user-namespace permission differences, discovered only after wasted build time; this affects local Guix build users and increases maintainer support burden diagnosing environment issues.

open_concerns: Whether the project wants to address unprivileged-daemon hazards this way at all is still being discussed in RFC issue #36239.

result.card: This draft PR adds a runtime warning in contrib/guix/guix-build when guix-daemon runs as a non-root user, plus INSTALL.md instructions to migrate back to a privileged daemon, aiming to save developers from confusing, hours-long build failures caused by unprivileged Guix daemon configurations. The problem is real per the linked RFC issue #36239, which discusses hazards of the modern unprivileged Guix daemon setup, but the PR's fix is only a developer convenience for local, non-substitute builds and does not touch release reproducibility. A maintainer, hebasto, asked to keep this as a draft until the RFC discussion in #36239 reaches rough consensus, since that could change the intended approach. No one has yet reviewed the code's substance. This is a small, self-contained, first-time-contributor change with no dependency stack conflicts.
